observations: Multiple rolls of electrical wire in red, black, and green colors.
The rolls are wrapped in transparent plastic packaging.
The brand name 'COLEMAN' is visible on the packaging tape of several rolls in photo 0.
Technical labels are attached to the rolls, but the text is too blurry to read.
A watermark for 'FUTURE EMPIRE ELECTRONICS' is present across the center of the image.

claims.evidence: The labels on the rolls are too blurry to confirm the length.
The specific gauge of the rolls in the photo cannot be read from the labels.
The internal material of the wire is not visible in the photos.

risks.risk: The specific gauge (thickness) of the wire is unknown, which significantly affects the price.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the label on a single roll showing the mm² measurement.

risks.risk: The wire core may be Copper Clad Aluminum (CCA) rather than pure copper.
risks.proof: A close-up photo or video of a cut wire end showing the color of the metal core.

risks.risk: The actual length of the roll may be less than the claimed 100m (e.g., a 'short' roll).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the label showing the length in meters.

risks.risk: The product may be a counterfeit version of the Coleman brand.
risks.proof: A photo of the holographic security seal or the SON registration number on the label.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the label on a single roll showing the gauge (mm²) and length (m).
Close-up photo of the wire core at a cut end to verify it is pure copper.
Photo of the holographic security seal on the packaging to verify authenticity.
response.reason: The gauge (thickness) of the wire is the primary factor for its price and is not legible in the photo. Furthermore, the seller is advertising a range of sizes (1mm to 10mm) rather than a specific item.
